literal_source_claim: The L^p boundedness of conjugate functions.
canonical_claim: For every exponent 1 < p < infinity there is a nonnegative constant C_p such that every complex-valued L^p function on the unit additive circle with Haar measure has an L^p conjugate function g, whose nth Fourier coefficient is -i sign(n) times that of f (and whose zero coefficient is zero), with norm at most C_p times the norm of f.
domain_and_universes: p : ENNReal; f and g are complex-valued Lp equivalence classes on AddCircle (1 : Real), using AddCircle.haarAddCircle; no universe parameters.
quantifiers: f in the source-specified L^p space
possibly a bound constant C_p depending only on p
hypotheses: integrability exponent lies strictly between 1 and infinity
f belongs to the chosen periodic L^p space
conclusion: The source-defined conjugate function exists in L^p and satisfies the source-specified L^p bound.
excluded_degenerate_cases: The strong-type endpoints p = 1 and p = infinity are excluded. The circle period is 1, scalars are complex, functions are Lp equivalence classes, and the Fourier multiplier sends the zero mode to zero. Principal-value and real-valued encodings receive no credit without later checked transports.
